preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide [j] to a palatalized voiced stop [dʲ]. In Samoyedic, Proto-Samoyedic word-initial *j is reflected by a palatalized stop in several daughters. Forest and Tundra Enets, which have a phonemic /dʲ/, show д- before the vowel in words such as дери (djeri) 'day' < *jalä and дю (dju) 'knot' < *jü, and Forest Nenets has дяԓя (dyałya) 'day', while Tundra Nenets keeps the glide (яля). Nganasan has the parallel outcome, but its phonology is usually described with a palatal stop /ɟ/, so it is filed under j > ɟ instead.

examples.to: Forest Enets дери (djeri), Tundra Enets дере (djere) 'day'
examples.note: Compare Tundra Nenets яля (yalya), which keeps the glide. The Proto-Samoyedic overview describes Enets as retaining *j; the dictionary forms (Janhunen 1977 via Wiktionary) show a palatalized stop.

examples.to: Forest and Tundra Enets дюʼ (djuʔ), дюр (djur)

examples.note: Forest Nenets contrasts palatalization but not voicing, so the reflex is a palatalized coronal stop.
